name: BMW M2 (F87)
engine: 3.0L turbo inline-six — N55 single-turbo (2016–2018) · S55 twin-turbo on the M2 Competition (2019–2021)
torque: 343 lb-ft @ 1,450–4,750 rpm (369 lb-ft on overboost) — N55 car; the Competition's S55 makes 406 lb-ft
reliability: 8/10 — the F87 M2 is widely called the purest modern M car, and it's also one of the more dependable, especially the original N55 single-turbo car. The N55's ownership items are minor and well-understood: a plastic charge pipe that cracks under boost (an easy aluminum swap), wastegate rattle from worn linkage, and the usual valve-cover/oil-pan gasket weeps. The 2019+ M2 Competition inherits the M3/M4's S55 twin-turbo and its single-bolt crank-hub concern — mostly a tuned/launch-control risk, but worth knowing. Either way, a stout, tossable, appreciating M coupe.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (compact performance coupe) · Maintenance ~$800/yr · Strong demand and 'last analog M' status keep resale high, manuals especially
popular_mods: An aluminum charge pipe — cheap insurance against the N55's known cracking failure
A tune (N55 or S55) — both respond strongly and safely to a quality flash
An intake and intercooler to keep temps down on repeated hard runs
On the S55 Competition, a crank-hub upgrade before pushing serious power or using launch control hard
Honest take: it's brilliant stock — sort the charge pipe and cooling, then a mild tune is all most owners ever need
oil_type: BMW LL-01 synthetic (0W-30 / 5W-30; a 5W-40 is common for track or hot climates)
oil_interval: Every 5,000–7,500 miles (short of BMW's condition-based interval)

generations.M2 (2016–2018, N55): The original — a short-wheelbase M coupe with the N55 single-turbo six (365 hp / 343 lb-ft, 369 on overboost) borrowed and strengthened from the M235i. Compact, communicative, and the enthusiast favorite.
generations.M2 Competition (2019–2021, S55): Swapped in the M3/M4-derived S55 twin-turbo for 405 hp / 406 lb-ft, with a stiffer front strut brace and cooling upgrades. The limited M2 CS (444 hp) capped the run as the collector's pick.

common_issues: N55 plastic charge pipe cracking under boost — near-universal aluminum upgrade
Wastegate rattle from a worn actuator/linkage on the N55
Valve-cover and oil-pan gasket oil weeps with age
S55 Competition inherits the single-bolt crank-hub slippage risk (mainly tuned/launch cars)
maintenance_tips: Fit an aluminum charge pipe early — the factory plastic one is a known weak point
Change oil every 5,000–7,500 miles with the correct LL-01 synthetic rather than stretching the CBS interval
On the S55 Competition, address the crank hub before high-power tunes or repeated launch-control use
Keep the cooling system healthy (water pump, thermostat) on any car that sees track use
Let the turbo six warm up before boost and cool briefly after hard runs
